fields.h1: Build a Language Quiz for Any Language and Level
fields.hero_description: Build a language quiz in any language that scores each player, places them by level, and saves answers to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Language Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A language quiz checks what someone knows about a language or about languages. Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions in the language you teach

Name the language, the level, and the topic, such as Spanish verbs in the past tense. Emergent writes each question with one right answer and three wrong ones of the same kind.
fields.feature_2:
Score bands that place each learner

Set the bands, such as 0 to 9 for Level 1 and 10 to 17 for Level 2, and the quiz shows each player the level they land in. Ask Emergent to draft the message for each band.
fields.feature_3:
Every answer tagged by skill

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the player, the question, and the skill it tests, such as verbs or vocabulary. Sort by skill to see what a class misses.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Players answer one question per screen, so a class can take the quiz on their phones in the first ten minutes of a lesson. Emergent puts no cap on how many people answer a quiz.
fields.feature_5:
A list of who fell below the pass mark

Set a pass mark, such as 12 of 15, and the app posts the name of anyone below it to a Slack channel. Send the list by email instead when only one teacher or trainer needs to see it.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain and your own code

Publish the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and add next term's questions.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Language Quiz With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Emergent builds the quiz as your own app. Each answer is stored in a database you own, and one prompt adds the next unit's questions.

plan.angle: The top 10 is all play: Britannica, JetPunk, Sporcle, BuzzFeed, Speechling and guess-the-language videos offer a language quiz to take, and none shows how to make one with your own questions, levels and results table. This page gives both: an 8-question world languages quiz to play on the page, every answer sourced, then four language quizzes that a language school, a Spanish teacher, a folk festival and a hotel run as their own app, each saving every answer to a table that shows who goes where and what people missed.
tab_stories: Bracewell Language School sends a 24-question French placement quiz to 58 new adult sign-ups, score bands put each one in Level 1, 2 or 3, and 27 land in Level 2, so the school opens a second Level 2 section.

A Spanish 2 teacher at Greywater High runs a 12-question past-tense quiz on phones in class, one question per screen, and 19 of 31 students miss the imperfect question, so she starts the next class with it.
The Oakhaven Folk Festival runs a guess-the-language booth where 340 visitors read one sentence per question and name the language, and only 51 of 340 name the Icelandic sentence.
Lantern Quay Hotel gives its 14 new front-desk hires a 15-question quiz on Spanish guest phrases, and a Slack message to #frontdesk-training lists the 4 who score under 12 of 15.
